GAME_TAGLINE: Floorball, five and a goalkeeper a side, to the real rules
MENU_QUICK_DESC: Pick two countries and face off
MENU_HOWTO_DESC: Controls, rules and the referees' signs
CUP_DESC: Sixteen nations: groups, play-offs and medals
PERIOD_NOTE: A match is three periods. The rules say 20 minutes each; shorter periods suit a phone.
DIFF_ROOKIE_DESC: Opponents slow to press and slow to shoot; goalkeepers beatable.
DIFF_CLUB_DESC: A good club side: they press the ball and punish loose passes.
DIFF_ELITE_DESC: Top league pace: quick passing, sharp goalkeepers.
DIFF_WORLD_DESC: The best national teams: every mistake ends in your net.
CLOCK_IFF_NOTE: The IFF rules: the clock stops at every whistle. Overtime is 10 minutes.
CLOCK_LEAGUE_NOTE: As many leagues play: the clock runs on through stoppages, except in the last three minutes. Overtime is 5 minutes.
SPEED_NOTE: Steady plays a little slower than real floorball, which is very fast on a small screen.
AUTO_SWITCH_NOTE: Without the ball, you take over the team-mate nearest to it.
GFX_NOTE: Low suits older phones; High adds shadows and a sharper picture.
GFX_LOWERED: Graphics lowered to keep the match smooth
FPS_NOTE_SAVER: About {n} frames a second at a lower resolution: the battery lasts longest.
FPS_NOTE_SMOOTH: {n} frames a second on your {hz} Hz screen.
FPS_NOTE_MAX: As many frames as your {hz} Hz screen shows: smoothest, most battery.
MOVE_BUTTONS_NOTE: Drag each button to where your thumb wants it.
ABOUT_DISCLAIMER: Floorstorm is not made, approved or endorsed by any floorball federation, league, club or player. National teams appear under their countries' names only.
LICENCES_INTRO: Floorstorm is built with the Godot Engine and free fonts. Their licences ask for these notices.
HOWTO_INTRO: You play one outfield player of your team; the rest of your team plays as a team does. The goalkeepers play themselves.
CTRL_MOVE_BODY: Put your left thumb down anywhere on the left of the screen and slide it: the joystick appears under it. Your player is the one with the yellow number.
CTRL_SHOOT_BODY: With the ball, SHOOT. Push the joystick up or down as you press to aim at a corner. From further out it is a slap shot: harder, less accurate.
CTRL_PASS_BODY: PASS goes to the team-mate in the joystick's direction, or the best one if you are not pushing it. You then play the player you passed to.
CTRL_SPRINT_BODY: Hold SPRINT to run flat out. It tires your player; a fresh line comes on about every fifty seconds.
CTRL_TACKLE_BODY: Without the ball, TACKLE plays your stick at the ball. From the front it often wins it. From behind, or on the stick, it is a free-hit; a trip or a slash is two minutes.
CTRL_SWITCH_BODY: SWITCH takes over the team-mate nearest the ball.
CTRL_RESTART_BODY: When your player takes one, the opponents stand 3 m back. Press PASS or SHOOT: a free-hit or hit-in must be a hit, and you may score straight from it.
CTRL_SHOOTOUT_BODY: From the centre spot the ball must keep moving toward the goal. Steer with the joystick and press SHOOT once: there is no rebound.
CTRL_PAUSE: Pause and the phone's Back button
CTRL_PAUSE_BODY: Back pauses the match and resumes it. From the pause menu: your one time-out, moving the buttons, sound, or leaving the match.
RULES_INTRO: Floorstorm follows the International Floorball Federation's Rules of the Game, the edition in force from 1 July 2026. The numbers are the rules'.
RULE_RINK_BODY: 40 by 20 metres inside boards 50 cm high with rounded corners. In front of each goal, the 4 by 5 m goal crease; inside it, the 1 by 2.5 m goalkeeper area. The goals are 160 cm wide and 115 cm high.
RULE_TEAMS_BODY: Up to 20 players a team, five outfield players and a goalkeeper on the rink. Players change at any time and as often as they like, but only in their team's own substitution zone.
RULE_TIME_BODY: Three periods of 20 minutes with 10-minute intervals; the teams change ends each interval. The clock stops at every whistle; leagues may run it, but never in the last three minutes.
RULE_FACEOFF_BODY: Each period and every restart after a goal begin at the centre spot. After other stoppages, the face-off is at the nearest face-off dot. Everyone else stands 3 m away.
RULE_HITIN_BODY: Over the boards, the team that did not touch it last hits it in, 1.5 m from the boards where it went out, never behind the goal line's extension. Opponents 3 m away. A goal may be scored straight from a hit-in.
RULE_FREEHIT_BODY: Taken where the offence happened, but never within 3.5 m of the goal crease or behind the goal line's extension. Opponents 3 m away, sticks included. It must be a hit, and it may go straight in.
RULE_STICK_BODY: No hitting, hooking, lifting or blocking an opponent's stick; no stick above the waist in the swing; no playing the ball above the knee; no stick or leg between an opponent's legs. Each is a free-hit; dangerous ones are two minutes.
RULE_BODY_BODY: Shoulder to shoulder only: no pushing, holding or obstructing. No playing the ball with the head or hands, jumping for it, or playing it sitting, lying or on two knees. The foot may play it below the knee, but a goal may not be kicked in.
RULE_GK_BODY: No stick. In his goal crease he may use his hands; outside it he plays as a field player without them. He may hold the ball 3 seconds at most. Since 2026 he may score with a throw.
RULE_GKAREA_BODY: Since 2026 no field player may pass through the goalkeeper area, and every field player must make a real effort not to collide with the goalkeeper or follow him to block his view.
RULE_GOALS_BODY: The whole ball over the goal line from the front, played correctly with a stick or thrown by the goalkeeper. Not kicked or headed in, and not after an offence by the attacking team. An own goal always counts.
RULE_PENALTIES_BODY: A minor bench penalty is 2 minutes, a major 5. A 10-minute personal penalty puts the player out and his team serves 2 minutes too. A match penalty puts the player out for good and his team serves 5 minutes. No more than two of a team's penalties run at once.
RULE_PP_BODY: A team a player down plays four against five. If the team with more players scores, the shortest 2-minute penalty ends; a 5-minute penalty never ends early.
RULE_PENSHOT_BODY: For an offence that stops a clear chance of a goal. From the centre spot, the ball always moving toward the goal; one shot, no rebound.
RULE_OT_BODY: When a match needs a winner: 10 minutes of overtime, the first goal wins. Then five different players a team take a penalty shot each, and then one a team until one scores and the other does not.
RULE_ADVANTAGE_BODY: If the fouled team keeps the ball, the referee lets play go on. For a penalty he raises an arm and whistles when the other team touches the ball; a goal in the meantime cancels a 2-minute penalty.
SIGNS_INTRO: Two referees, equal in authority, follow play along the long sides. After the whistle a referee first shows the consequence, then the offence when it is needed.
SIGN_FREE_HIT_BODY: An arm out level, pointing the way the free-hit goes; the foot marks the spot.
SIGN_HIT_IN_BODY: An arm pointing down toward the floor, the way the hit-in goes.
SIGN_ADVANTAGE_BODY: An arm out forward and up, the way the play goes, and the call: advantage!
SIGN_DELAYED_BODY: An arm straight up, held until the penalised team touches the ball.
SIGN_GOAL_BODY: Pointing to the centre spot, where play starts again.
SIGN_NO_GOAL_BODY: Both arms swept out to the sides.
SIGN_PEN2_BODY: An arm up, two fingers shown.
SIGN_PEN5_BODY: An arm up, the open hand showing five.
SIGN_PENALTY_SHOT_BODY: Pointing to the centre spot, then the arms crossed above the head.
OFF_GK_HOLD: Goalkeeper held the ball too long
INTERVAL_NOTE: The teams change ends. Ten minutes' interval in the hall; here, carry on when you are ready.
OVERTIME_NOTE: Level after three periods: sudden victory, the first goal wins. Then penalty shots.
CUP_INTRO: Sixteen nations as the world championships are played: four groups of four, play-offs, quarter-finals, semi-finals and the medal matches. Pick your country.
CUP_OUT: Your country is out. The tournament goes on without you.
GROUP_NOTE: Group matches may end in a draw: two points for a win, one for a draw.
KNOCKOUT_NOTE: Win or go home: level after 60 minutes means overtime, then penalty shots.
